authors: Toshiyuki Kanmachi | Ryusuke Tokuno | Kiyoshi Ohishi
title: Anti-Windup Control Considering the Acceleration Torque Component for the Speed Control System of an AC Servo
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 137(5), 427-436, 2017
evidence: A 500 W speed servo has a 13.9 A q-axis limiter. Table 2 reports mean full-load acceleration overshoot of 93.6 rpm with conventional anti-windup and 38.6 rpm with the weighted acceleration-torque method.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: The comparator is speed overshoot. The acceleration-torque term and load-current estimate should not be converted to independently measured shaft torque.

authors: Kazuhide Kaneko | Kiyoshi Ohishi
title: Design Method of Limitation Compensator Maintaining Response Performance for PI Speed Control System of SPMSM
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 133(5), 526-535, 2013
evidence: The feedback of the difference across the current limiter is shaped using motor dynamics. Hardware step-speed responses are shown even when the assumed torque constant or inertia differs by ±30%.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: Figs 11–13 are simulations; the robustness tests alter assumed motor parameters, not the physical load calibration.

authors: Masaki Sazawa | Takahiro Yamada | Kiyoshi Ohishi | Seiichiro Katsura
title: Anti-Windup Algorithm with Priority to Proportinal Control Output of Speed PI Controller for Position Servo System
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 128(3), 208-214, 2008
evidence: On a position step, proportional-priority anti-windup had zero measured speed overshoot under constant full load versus 9.09% with integrator limiting. At three times the inertia, its overshoot was 4.55%.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: The experiment compares load conditions, controller components, position and speed. The tables do not provide synchronized torque-sensor traces.

authors: Xing Gao | Satosi Komada | Takamasa Hori
title: A Method of Wind-up Restraint Control of Servo System with Torque Saturation
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 120(11), 1321-1327, 2000
evidence: A torque saturation model inside the disturbance observer reduces observer-induced instability. Predictive torque reversal and its modification are evaluated in intermittent and repetitive motion.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: The predictive torque waveform is a control quantity. Figs 9–11 give experimental motion evidence, with no freely verified machine-readable shaft-torque capture.

authors: Kiyoshi Ohishi | Emiko Hayasaka | Tetsuaki Nagano | Masaya Harakawa
title: Speed Servo System Considering Voltage Saturation of Indiredt Vector Control System
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 122(2), 120-127, 2002
evidence: An induction-motor speed servo compensates the current regulator for the voltage the inverter can actually apply, and adjusts the indirect vector-control phase. The paper alternates experimental and simulated step-response panels.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: Experimental speed response and phase-voltage limitation address the drive side; independent shaft-torque observations were not recovered. The landing-page title misspells Indirect as Indiredt.

authors: Youichi Egashira | Kiyoshi Ohishi
title: Speed Control Method for PM Motor Considering Voltage Saturation
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 126(2), 206-207, 2006
evidence: On a 200 W eight-pole motor under rated load, the authors step from zero to 3000 rpm. The revised voltage-saturation compensation settles 150 ms faster than the conventional method in their reported experiment.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: The voltage vector reflects inverter feasibility. It is not an observed motor-current clamp or a shaft-torque series.

authors: Takayuki Miyajima | Hiroshi Fujimoto | Masami Fujitsuna
title: Current Control for SPMSM in Field-Weakening Region Based on Final-State Control
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 132(8), 794-801, 2012
evidence: Final-state feedforward current control in field weakening is tested on an SPMSM. Figure 6 gives d/q measured responses for two conventional schemes and horizons of 40 and 49 for the proposed schemes.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: Figure 9 explicitly uses simulation for the transient voltage-limit circle. This does not measure a torque plateau.

authors: Jun Kitajima | Kiyoshi Ohishi | Yoshiaki Seki
title: Rapid and Stable Speed Response Based on Current Differential Signal and Priority Amplitude Method of SVM in Flux-Weakening Region of SPMSM
source_version: Publisher version, IEEJ Journal of Industry Applications 4(3), 107-115, 2015
evidence: At 25% applied load the combination scheme and comparator both settled in 129 ms, while peak d-axis current fell from 0.98 to 0.67 A. At 75% load both settled in 188 ms and the corresponding amplitudes were 0.99 and 0.71 A.
rights: J-STAGE free public PDF; copyright IEEJ. Source linked, no redistribution of PDF.
limitations: These data distinguish savings in d-axis current from faster settling. Load percentage is an experimental condition rather than sampled shaft torque.

authors: Michal Gierczynski | Rafal Jakubowski | Emil Kupiec | Lukasz Jan Niewiara | Tomasz Tarczewski | Lech M. Grzesiak
title: Identification of the Parameters of the Highly Saturated Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM): Selected Problems of Accuracy
source_version: Publisher version, Energies 17(23), 6096, 2024
locator: Sec. 2 test bench and Fig. 2; Sec. 3 Figs 17–18; supplement S1
evidence: A KTR DATAFLEX 42/200 measures shaft torque while a separate drive maintains roughly 550 rpm. The public supplement contains d/q requested and measured current grids plus torque values in four workbooks.
limitations: The command grid is a steady operating-point design. It contains no before-and-after limiter signals or command time base. See current-grid-source.json for independently decoded results.

authors: Wojciech Pietrowski | Magdalena Puskarczyk | Jan Szymenderski
title: Analysis of PMSM Torque Waveform Discrepancies in a Hardware-in-the-Loop Environment
source_version: Publisher version, Electronics 15(17), 3946, 2026
locator: Sec. 3.2, Tables 2, 3 and 5; Data Availability Statement
evidence: An affine fit matches three mean HiL torques to dynamometer means by construction at 20, 100 and 200 rpm. Raw Pearson coefficients for the steady-state torque waves are −0.043, −0.128 and −0.150.
limitations: Matching mean torque leaves the local ripple poorly reproduced. Physical waveforms are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.

authors: Mingzhan Chen | Jie Zhang | Jie Hong
title: Research on Torque Estimation Methods for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Considering Dynamic Inductance Variations
source_version: Publisher version, Energies 19(2), 346, 2026
locator: Sec. 5 experimental platform and Fig. 3; Figs 4–10 and Tables 3–4
evidence: The authors compare a dynamometer-loaded motor estimate with a torque sensor. At 1800 rpm they test both a ramp to 70 N·m and a step to that load. The inductance reference combines offline frequency response with finite-element analysis.
limitations: The torque reference and inductance reference come from different procedures. A load step does not reveal a controller current limit.

authors: Yu-Ting Lin | Jonq-Chin Hwang | Jyun-You Chen
title: Parameter Identification of a Six-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Maximum Torque per Ampere Control
source_version: Publisher version, Energies 19(19), 4658, 2026
evidence: A dynamometer controls speed while torque references stay at 0, 0.25, 0.5 or 1 per unit. At full reference the mean measured torque is 1349.3 N·m at standstill and 1333.4 N·m at 600 rpm.
limitations: The table averages one second. Motor-terminal voltage is reconstructed. The article makes the underlying data available on request.

authors: Jilei Xing | Junzhi Zhang | Xingming Zhuang | Yao Xu
title: Online Inductance Identification of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Independent of Rotor Position Information
source_version: Publisher version, World Electric Vehicle Journal 15(1), 35, 2024
evidence: A preassembled resolver independently checks a sensorless identification method. The MCU, power analyser and oscilloscope supply experimental observations. Offline hot/cold resistance and flux lookups enter the estimator.
limitations: The sensitivity of the d/q estimate to specified angular offsets in Fig. 3 is simulated; avoid treating those percentages as real shaft-torque error. Data on request.

authors: Jinyu Wang | Qiang Miao | Xiaomin Zhou | Lipeng Sun | Dawei Gao | Haifeng Lu
title: Current Control Method of Vehicle Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control
source_version: Publisher version, World Electric Vehicle Journal 14(1), 2, 2022
evidence: The dynamometer regulates speed. At 200 rpm, published tests for large and small torque steps compare d/q current waveforms from PI and active-disturbance-rejection control.
limitations: The plotted ordinate is current. A torque step in the caption identifies the applied demand and does not supply an independent measured output-torque trace.

authors: Zimou Chen | Zhe Wang
title: Development of a Dual-Mode Measurement and Control System with Energy Feedback Optimization for a Retrofitted NEV Powertrain Dynamometer
source_version: Publisher version, World Electric Vehicle Journal 17(9), 476, 2026
evidence: A motor-side flange and a Kistler 4503B are fused, using the flange below 10 Hz for cross-calibration. The regenerating front-end current setting was raised from 80% to 95% of rating.
limitations: This is a regenerative AFE limit, distinct from a post-limit motor torque command. The authors report forward rotation only, with data on reasonable request.

authors: Peng Wang | Z. Q. Zhu | Zhibin Feng
title: Online Parameter Identification of SPMSMs Under Sensorless Control Cancelling Influence of Position Error With Torque Measurements
source_version: Publisher version, IET Electric Power Applications 20(1), e70185, 2026
locator: Secs 4.2–4.3, Fig. 8 and Eq. 27; Sec. 5 experimental verification
evidence: Reaction torque from four LCKD-10 force sensors around the stator support provides an independent constraint in the 600 W generator experiment. The authors choose 5-degree offset injections to identify the electrical parameters.
limitations: The derivation excludes strong saliency and interior PM machines. Identification under angle perturbation does not establish output clipping.

authors: Getnet Ayele Kebede | Anton Royanto Ahmad | Shao-Chun Lee | Chyi-Yeu Lin
title: Decoupled Six-Axis Force–Moment Sensor with a Novel Strain Gauge Arrangement and Error Reduction Techniques
source_version: Publisher version, Sensors 19(13), 3012, 2019
evidence: The authors zero voltages on the unloaded calibration jig and subsequently offset the installed tool reading. Table 5 gives absolute force-axis measurement errors of 0.61%, 0.37% and 0.58% and moment-axis errors of 1.78%, 1.74% and 1.45%.
limitations: A pre-task offset removes the wrench at the zeroing pose, including payload effects. This is not a longitudinal drift measurement.

authors: Ahmed Joubair | Long Zhao | Pascal Bigras | Ilian Bonev
title: Use of a Force-Torque Sensor for Self-Calibration of a 6-DOF Medical Robot
source_version: Publisher version, Sensors 16(6), 798, 2016
evidence: Gravity-induced wrist wrenches are proposed to calibrate kinematics simultaneously with tool/sensor frames. The observability study compares pose selections and evaluates position error in the target workspace.
limitations: The conclusions explicitly leave experimental validation to future work. This is a simulation-only comparator despite the experimental-sounding title.

authors: Ryuichiro Koike | Sho Sakaino | Toshiaki Tsuji
title: Hysteresis Compensation in Force/Torque Sensors Using Time Series Information
source_version: Europe PMC full text, Sensors 19(19), 2019
evidence: A robot rotates a 3D-printed resin six-axis sensor with a known weight. Strain history helped linear regression under both training-set sizes; with less data it increased error for the NN and hybrid models.
limitations: External force is calculated from load and kinematics. Hysteresis under known loading differs from zero drift under a stationary unloaded wrist.

authors: Anton Royanto Ahmad | Terrence Wynn | Chyi-Yeu Lin
title: A Comprehensive Design of Six-Axis Force/Moment Sensor
source_version: Europe PMC full text, Sensors 21(13), 2021
evidence: An ATI AXIA 80 establishes comparison loads on the same jig. With 32 gauges and commercial acquisition the largest reported measurement error is 1.13% on My and largest crosstalk is 1.20% on Mx.
limitations: Jig validation used the same weight plates in succession. Do not infer a synchronized reference during motion or independent contact ground truth.

authors: Hubert Gattringer | Andreas Müller | Philip Hoermandinger
title: Design and Calibration of Robot Base Force/Torque Sensors and Their Application to Non-Collocated Admittance Control for Automated Tool Changing
source_version: Europe PMC full text, Sensors 21(9), 2021
locator: Secs 2–4; Fig. 5, Eqs 8 and 14 and discussion
evidence: Three load cells or a four-spoke base plate estimate the vertical force and two horizontal moments during quasi-static tool changing. Calibration uses robot torque and inertia information.
limitations: Three observable wrench components and base mounting limit transfer to wrist six-axis zero-bias estimation. Dynamic calibration is left open.

authors: Lei Yao | Qingguang Gao | Dailin Zhang | Wanpeng Zhang | Youping Chen
title: An Integrated Compensation Method for the Force Disturbance of a Six-Axis Force Sensor in Complex Manufacturing Scenarios
source_version: Europe PMC full text, Sensors 21(14), 2021
evidence: A neural zero predictor is trained from 9,966 unloaded items; least-squares load compensation uses 15 arm orientations. Table A2 gives rotation vectors, and Table 3 compares zero-point errors by axis.
limitations: Fifteen tabulated poses do not reconstruct the training time series. The authors make data available on request.

authors: Diyun Wen | Jiangtao Xiao | Yu Xie | Tao Luo | Jinhui Zhang | Wei Zhou
title: A Universal Tool Interaction Force Estimation Approach for Robotic Tool Manipulation
source_version: Europe PMC full text, Sensors 25(21), 2025
evidence: For four tools spanning 0.89–3.51 kg, a dynamic model and a spiking network compensate tool wrench and residual error. In the noncontact evaluation the Mz RMSE falls from 0.031 to 0.008 N·m with the network.
limitations: That RMSE uses assumed zero external contact force. A rigid grasp and a single sensor configuration limit claims about loaded dynamic contact or long-term drift.

authors: Seung Yeon Lee | Jae Yoon Sim | Dong-Yeop Seok | Yong Bum Kim | Jaeyoon Shim | Uikyum Kim | Hyouk Ryeol Choi
title: A Redundant-Sensing-Based Six-Axis Force/Torque Sensor Enabling Compactness and High Sensitivity
source_version: Europe PMC full text, Sensors 26(3), 2026
evidence: A 16-cell capacitive design is calibrated against a six-axis reference in a transformed frame. Table 2 gives a ±100 N force range and ±0.5 N·m torque range, with three different torque resolutions.
limitations: The reported crosstalk and hysteresis are full-scale-normalized metrics. They do not measure thermal zero drift. Numerical data on request.
